prospects.thesis: Lockheed is the premier prime contractor with dominant franchises in F-35, missile defense (THAAD, PAC-3), and hypersonics — all directly funded by the FY27 defense budget uplift and sustained Ukraine/Israel/Taiwan replenishment demand. Reasonable 1.7x P/S for a $134B cap name with bullish options flow and institutional accumulation suggests smart money is positioning ahead of contract awards. Pullback from recent highs offers an attractive risk/reward with 10Y yields easing.

SAIC is a pure-play IT services contractor to DoD and federal civilian agencies, benefiting from digital modernization, JADC2, and classified AI/cloud migration budgets. The +10.2% 1M move on bullish institutional flow signals a breakout, yet at 0.8x P/S it remains one of the cheapest ways to play defense-tech digitization. Differentiated sub-niche from the primes — services/software exposure rather than platforms.

HII is the sole builder of U.S. nuclear aircraft carriers and one of two Virginia-class submarine yards — an irreplaceable asset as the Navy accelerates shipbuilding to counter China's naval expansion. AUKUS funding and multi-year submarine block buys provide decade-long revenue visibility; +7.0% 1M momentum with bullish institutional positioning confirms the thesis is gaining traction. Diversified from aerospace/missile primes via naval sub-niche exposure.

Broadcom is the critical custom-silicon (XPU) partner for hyperscaler AI buildouts and dominates AI networking via Tomahawk/Jericho switching — the two highest-growth pockets of the AI capex cycle outside of merchant GPUs. Bullish options and institutional flow signal continued accumulation, and VMware integration synergies are now flowing through margins. Essential semiconductor diversification away from the watchlist's NVDA/MU exposure.

AMD's MI350/MI400 roadmap and ZT Systems acquisition position it as the credible #2 AI accelerator vendor, with hyperscaler diversification away from NVDA accelerating. The -2.4% 1M pullback against bullish options and institutional flow creates a constructive setup, but at 19x P/S execution risk is elevated. Only non-defense AI pure-play on the list offering meaningful theme diversification.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Here's what's interesting in this flow: big money is piling into rate-sensitive sectors — Real Estate and Utilities are flashing the most bullish signals, which almost always means institutions are betting the Fed cuts rates sooner or deeper than consensus thinks, and that fits with the softer economic data we've been seeing plus the political pressure on Powell from the administration to ease. The Tech bid with unusual volume tells me the AI infrastructure trade isn't dead — it's getting refreshed, likely tied to continued federal AI spending, chip subsidies, and the lack of any real antitrust teeth from the current DOJ. On the flip side, the heavy hedging in Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Energy, and especially Consumer Staples (that 3.86 put/call is loud) tells you smart money is positioning for a consumer slowdown and margin squeeze — tariffs are raising input costs for staples and discretionary, while Energy bearishness likely reflects demand worries plus the administration's "drill baby drill" supply push keeping a lid on crude. Historically this rotation — defensives and rate-plays up, cyclicals and consumer down — precedes a 1-3 month period where the market narrative shifts from "soft landing" to "growth scare," even if indexes hold up. The contradiction worth noting: Healthcare is getting dumped hard (7x volume on bearish bets) even though it's usually defensive — that's a tell that drug pricing executive orders, RFK Jr.'s HHS agenda, and Medicare negotiation expansion are scaring institutions in a way headlines are underplaying. The non-obvious takeaway: credit spreads are widening and HYG puts are off the charts while investment-grade LQD is bid — that's the bond market quietly saying a credit event or default cycle is brewing
